questions.stem: State the equation for the acid-catalysed iodination of propanone.
questions.modelAnswer: CH3COCH3 + I2 gives CH3COCH2I and HI, with dilute sulfuric acid as catalyst.

questions.stem: State what is measured before the investigation begins.
questions.modelAnswer: The absorbances of a set of standard iodine solutions, to obtain the calibration curve.

questions.stem: Explain why absorbance can track iodine concentration during the run.
questions.modelAnswer: Iodine is the coloured species being consumed, and absorbance is proportional to a coloured species' concentration, so each logged reading gives the iodine concentration at that instant once the calibration curve is applied.

questions.stem: A student mixes propanone and acid, then adds iodine fifteen seconds before starting the data logger. Comment on the consequence.
questions.modelAnswer: The reaction ran unlogged for fifteen seconds, so the earliest data are missing; the curve still exists but its opening section must be extrapolated, and the missing window weakens any early-gradient reading.

options.explanation: The catalyst is fixed, not tabulated per run.

options.explanation: The falling concentration is the whole point.

questions.stem: State the gradient calculation demonstrated at 300 seconds.
questions.modelAnswer: 0.0069 divided by 590, giving 1.17 x 10^-5 mol dm^-3 s^-1.

questions.stem: State what the specimen results table and its graph record.
questions.modelAnswer: The iodine concentration falling as the reaction proceeds, against time.

questions.stem: Explain why a tangent, rather than a chord, is used to read the rate at 300 seconds.
questions.modelAnswer: A chord averages the rate over an interval, while a tangent touches the curve at one instant, so only the tangent's gradient is the instantaneous rate at exactly 300 seconds.

questions.stem: Two tangents on the same results curve give 1.17 x 10^-5 at 300 s and a smaller value at 600 s. What does the shrinkage suggest about the order in iodine?
questions.modelAnswer: The rate falls as iodine concentration falls, so the rate depends on iodine concentration - behaviour pointing to a positive order in iodine rather than zero order.
